c.tagline: A Catalan medieval jewel of pastel riverside houses, Jewish quarter alleys, and Game of Thrones filming spots

card: Widely accepted; cash useful for small old-town shops and markets

taxi.fare: Metered, roughly €3.40 flag fall plus per-km rate
taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard and reliable

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-style emergency number that connects to police, fire, and ambulance

walk: The old town is compact, hilly in places, and very walkable; most sights are within a 20-minute walk of each other

safety.safety: Very safe city, popular for day trips and short stays
safety.crime: Petty theft in crowded tourist spots is the main concern

hood_landmark.Barri Vell (Old Town): Girona Cathedral and its 90-step Baroque staircase
hood_landmark.Mercadal: Plaça de la Independència's neoclassical arcades
hood_landmark.Pedret: The Romanesque Sant Pere de Galligants monastery

avoid.reason: Pickpockets target the packed old-town lanes during Temps de Flors and summer weekends; otherwise usual city awareness.

hood_desc: The hilltop medieval core with the cathedral, city walls, and narrow stone lanes; the essential base for any visit and a Game of Thrones filming location.
The lively 19th-century civic center across the river, with cafes, shops, and the colorful Onyar riverside facades.
A quieter residential expansion beyond the old town, useful for longer stays and local-feeling apartments.
A low-key riverside area northeast of the old town with the Romanesque Sant Pere monastery, mostly of interest to history-focused visitors.

water.note: Tap water is safe, though many locals drink bottled for the chlorinated taste.

transit.sys: TMG (Transports Municipals de Girona) urban bus network
transit.pay: Cash or contactless card on board; rechargeable travel card available
transit.note: The old town is best explored on foot; buses mainly serve outlying neighborhoods and the train/bus station

transport.air: Girona-Costa Brava Airport (GRO), about 15 min away; Barcelona El Prat (BCN) is a larger option roughly 1.5 hr away
transport.train: High-speed AVE and regional Rodalies trains connect to Barcelona (under 40 min) and France
transport.bus: Sagalés and ALSA coaches connect to Barcelona, the Costa Brava, and the Pyrenees
transport.car: Easy via the AP-7 motorway; the old town is pedestrian-only

airport.name: Girona-Costa Brava Airport
airport.transport: Airport bus, taxi, or rental car

net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: A Movistar, Vodafone, or Orange tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory; rounding up is appreciated for guides and tours
tip.r: 5-10% for good service, not expected at casual bars

landmarks: Girona Cathedral (Catedral de Santa Maria)
Crowning a monumental Baroque staircase, this cathedral boasts the world's widest Gothic nave and starred as the Great Sept in Game of Thrones.
Cases de l'Onyar (Houses on the Onyar)
Girona's postcard: a wall of ochre, coral and mustard houses rising sheer from the river, best framed from the red Eiffel Bridge.
El Call (Jewish Quarter)
One of Europe's best-preserved medieval Jewish quarters, a shadowy tangle of stone stairways and courtyards inhabited by a thriving community until 1492.
Passeig de la Muralla (City Walls Walk)
Stride the ramparts of Girona's Carolingian and medieval walls for rooftop, cathedral and Pyrenees views along the old town's entire eastern flank.
Pont de les Peixateries Velles (Eiffel Bridge)
This red lattice footbridge over the Onyar was built by Gustave Eiffel's company in 1877, shortly before the tower that made him famous.
Arab Baths (Banys Àrabs)
A beautifully preserved 12th-century Romanesque bathhouse whose octagonal columned pool and skylit lantern evoke Moorish and Roman bathing traditions.
Basilica of Sant Feliu
Girona's first cathedral, with its landmark truncated spire, guards Roman and early-Christian sarcophagi and the Gothic tomb of Saint Narcissus.
Monastery of Sant Pere de Galligants
A superb 12th-century Benedictine abbey whose sculpted cloister and stout bell tower now house Girona's archaeology museum.
Museum of Jewish History (Museu d'Història dels Jueus)
Set in the former synagogue complex, this affecting museum illuminates Sephardic life, kabbalist scholarship and the expulsion of Girona's Jews.
Rambla de la Llibertat and Plaça de la Independència
Girona's arcaded promenade and neoclassical porticoed square hum with café terraces, Saturday flower stalls and the evening passeig.

train.note: Girona sits on the high-speed line between Barcelona and the French border, so the cross-border AVE and TGV services actually stop here - you can board directly for Perpignan, Montpellier, Lyon, Marseille or Paris without going via Barcelona. Domestic AVE trains reach Barcelona Sants in 38 minutes and Madrid in about 3h30. The high-speed station is next to the older Rodalies station a short walk from the centre.

bus.note: The bus station is directly beneath the railway station. Sagalés and Teisa run the useful local services out to the Costa Brava beaches at Tossa de Mar, Lloret and Cadaqués, and there is a direct airport bus to Barcelona. International coaches mostly route through Barcelona.

ferry.note: Girona is inland on the river Onyar with no port, so there are no ferries. The nearest sailings are from Barcelona, about 100 km south, with Grimaldi and GNV services to Italy and Morocco.

half.name: Tossa de Mar
half.blurb: Costa Brava fishing town with a walled medieval quarter, Vila Vella, perched above a curved sandy beach.

half.name: Figueres
half.blurb: Home to the Dalí Theatre-Museum, a surrealist building the artist designed himself to house his own collection.

half.name: Besalú
half.blurb: Medieval village centered on a fortified Romanesque bridge over the Fluvià River, with a preserved Jewish quarter and mikveh.

half.name: Cadaqués
half.blurb: Whitewashed fishing village on a rocky Costa Brava cove where Salvador Dalí lived and painted for decades.

half.name: Banyoles
half.blurb: Lakeside town built around Estany de Banyoles, a spring-fed lake used for the 1992 Olympic rowing events.
